title: A Push for Traffic Stop Reform

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯 DealBook 报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的领导人，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》

sentences.en: York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Last year, a Times investigation found that minor traffic stops are far more lethal than anyone thought.
sentences.zh: 去年，《纽约时报》的一项调查发现，轻微交通违规拦截造成的致命后果远比人们想象的要严重得多。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, David Kirkpatrick, on the efforts to cut back on such stops and how a rise in violent crime threatens those reforMs. It's Monday, April 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事大卫·柯克帕特里克将讲述减少此类拦截的努力，以及暴力犯罪的上升如何威胁到这些改革。今天是4月25日，星期一。

sentences.en: David, last time we talked, you and our colleagues had just released this sweeping investigation into traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 大卫，上次我们交谈时，你和我们的同事刚刚发布了这项关于交通拦截的深度调查。

sentences.en: Remind us what you guys found.
sentences.zh: 请提醒我们你们发现了什么。

sentences.en: So criminologists have known for a while that traffic stops, especially for minor violations,
sentences.zh: 犯罪学家早就知道，交通拦截，尤其是针对轻微违规的拦截，

sentences.en: disproportionately affect Black people and people of color.
sentences.zh: 对黑人和有色人种的影响是不成比例的。

sentences.en: Those people are much more likely to get pulled over for trivial reasons.
sentences.zh: 这些人因为琐碎的原因被拦下的可能性要大得多。

sentences.en: So what my colleagues Steve Eater and Kim Barker and I added to that in our reporting last year was a sense of the death toll.
sentences.zh: 所以，我和我的同事史蒂夫·伊特和金·巴克在去年的报道中补充的是关于死亡人数的统计。

sentences.en: We found that over the previous five years, a total of more than 400 unarmed motorists who were not under pursuit for any violent
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在过去五年里，总共有超过400名手无寸铁的驾驶员，在没有因任何暴力

sentences.en: crime ended up killed by a police officer who had pulled them over.
sentences.zh: 犯罪而被追捕的情况下，最终被拦下他们的警察杀害。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I remember you really dug into why those incidents so frequently go wrong.
sentences.zh: 我记得你深入探讨了为什么这些事件会如此频繁地出错。

sentences.en: Well, at the core of it is the widespread belief among police that pulling over cars is exceptionally dangerous to the police.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其核心在于警察中普遍存在的一种信念，即拦车对警察来说极其危险。

sentences.en: Now, that's not really true.
sentences.zh: 但这其实并不属实。

sentences.en: In fact, if you look at the total number of cars that police pull over, there really is not a greater risk at any given stop to the police officer
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你看看警察拦车的总数，在任何一次拦截中，警察面临的风险其实并不比

sentences.en: than there is in a lot of other activities that police engage in.
sentences.zh: 他们在执行的其他许多任务中所面临的风险更大。

sentences.en: And yet, nonetheless, police are trained to go into these encounters ready to defend their lives, that their lives are on the line.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管如此，警察在接受训练时仍被要求在进行这些接触时做好保卫生命的准备，认为他们的生命正处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And that can lead to a kind of extra aggression.
sentences.zh: 这可能导致一种额外的攻击性。

sentences.en: And since our investigation, we've seen this pattern continue.
sentences.zh: 自我们的调查以来，我们看到这种模式仍在继续。

sentences.en: A long stream of seemingly innocuous traffic stops ending in the death of a motoriSt.
sentences.zh: 一连串看似无害的交通拦截最终导致了驾驶员的死亡。

sentences.en: We want to get right to our top story tonight.
sentences.zh: 我们想直接进入今晚的头条新闻。

sentences.en: The most recent example is in Grand Rapids, Michigan, of Patrick Lioia.
sentences.zh: 最近的一个例子发生在密歇根州大急流城，涉及帕特里克·利奥亚。

sentences.en: Pulled over, police say, because his license plate did not match the car.
sentences.zh: 据警方称，他被拦下是因为他的车牌与车辆不符。

sentences.en: Here is a 26-year-old black man who was pulled over for what the officer said were mismatched license plates.
sentences.zh: 这是一名26岁的黑人男子，他因为警察所说的车牌不匹配而被拦下。

sentences.en: Under public pressure, police have since released four videos of the incident.
sentences.zh: 在公众压力下，警方此后公布了四段关于该事件的视频。

sentences.en: The driver tried to flee.
sentences.zh: 司机试图逃跑。

sentences.en: The officer pursued him.
sentences.zh: 警察追赶他。

sentences.en: There was a brief scuffle, struggle for the officer's taser.
sentences.zh: 发生了一场短暂的扭打，争夺警察的泰瑟枪。

sentences.en: And seconds later, the officer shot him in the back of the head.
sentences.zh: 几秒钟后，警察朝他的后脑勺开了一枪。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: So that Grand Rapids, Michigan case sounds like exactly what you guys were investigating.
sentences.zh: 所以密歇根州大急流城的那个案子听起来和你调查的情况完全一样。

sentences.en: A really stark example of it.
sentences.zh: 一个非常鲜明的例子。

sentences.en: Yeah, it really is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: We saw example after example that unfolded in a very similar way.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了一个又一个以非常相似的方式展开的例子。

sentences.en: The motorist, for whatever reason, tries to flee.
sentences.zh: 司机无论出于什么原因试图逃跑。

sentences.en: The officer takes that flight as a sign of aggression.
sentences.zh: 警察将这种逃跑视为一种攻击信号。

sentences.en: The officer tries to pursue.
sentences.zh: 警察试图追捕。

sentences.en: And somehow, in a matter of seconds, it's escalated to the killing of the driver.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，在几秒钟内，事态升级为对司机的杀戮。

sentences.en: And, you know, in this case, it's kicked off protests again in Grand Rapids.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在这个案例中，它再次在大急流城引发了抗议。

sentences.en: And it's really kind of restarted a national conversation about these low-level traffic stops and their disproportionate impact on people of color.
sentences.zh: 它实际上重新开启了全国关于这些低级别交通拦截及其对有色人种不成比例影响的讨论。

sentences.en: So tell me what's changed since your investigation was published.
sentences.zh: 那么，请告诉我自你们的调查发表以来发生了什么变化。

sentences.en: Well, somewhat surprisingly to me, we're seeing a really broad rethinking of the way police do traffic stops in lots of places around the country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我有些惊讶的是，我们看到全国许多地方对警察进行交通拦截的方式进行了非常广泛的反思。

sentences.en: I mean, just to put it in perspective, the current approach to traffic stops has been around since the early 1980s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从宏观角度来看，目前的交通拦截方法自20世纪80年代初以来就一直存在。

sentences.en: There were three things at that time that led people to stop more cars.
sentences.zh: 当时有三件事导致人们拦截了更多的车辆。

sentences.en: One was a rise in crime rates.
sentences.zh: 一是犯罪率的上升。

sentences.en: The second was a responding shift on the part of police towards more proactive policing.
sentences.zh: 二是警察方面转向更主动的警务工作。

sentences.en: That is, they weren't going to just sit around and wait for the 911 call.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们不会只是坐着等待911报警电话。

sentences.en: They were going to try to go out and catch the criminals proactively.
sentences.zh: 他们会主动出击去抓捕罪犯。

sentences.en: And that included by pulling over cars.
sentences.zh: 这包括通过拦车来实现。

sentences.en: And the third thing is the advent of in-car computer systems that the police could use to try to run down plates and see whether they had a cause
sentences.zh: 第三件事是车载计算机系统的出现，警察可以用它来查询车牌，看看他们是否有理由

sentences.en: or even a pretext to pull over a car they might see on the road.
sentences.zh: 甚至只是借口来拦截他们在路上看到的车辆。

sentences.en: And all the three of these things combined to make what are now known as pretextual stops a real cornerstone of policing.
sentences.zh: 这三件事结合在一起，使得现在所谓的“借口性拦截”成为警务工作的真正基石。

sentences.en: That is, where the officer pulls over a car for a really minor reasons, like a broken taillight.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，警察以非常微小的理由（如尾灯破损）拦下一辆车。

sentences.en: But what they're really after is just to look around the car and see if they can see drugs or an expired warrant or guns or some evidence of a crime.
sentences.zh: 但他们真正想要的是环顾车内，看看是否能发现毒品、未决逮捕令、枪支或犯罪证据。

sentences.en: And what's happening now is that a variety of different jurisdictions in different ways are trying to rethink their approach to these kinds of traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 现在发生的情况是，各种不同的司法管辖区正以不同的方式试图重新思考他们处理此类交通拦截的方法。

sentences.en: And our investigation into the death toll from these stops in some places has even played a part in that rethinking.
sentences.zh: 我们对这些拦截造成的死亡人数的调查，在某些地方甚至在这一反思中发挥了作用。

sentences.en: When the Pittsburgh City Council passed a law banning low-level traffic stops, for example, the text of the legislation quoted our reporting.
sentences.zh: 例如，当匹兹堡市议会通过一项禁止低级别交通拦截的法律时，立法文本中引用了我们的报道。

sentences.en: So who's behind these moves in cities like Pittsburgh?
sentences.zh: 那么，在匹兹堡这样的城市，谁在推动这些举措？

sentences.en: Well, it's different people in different places around the country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，全国各地的情况各不相同。

sentences.en: In some places, it's the city councils.
sentences.zh: 在一些地方，是市议会。

sentences.en: Philadelphia in March became the first big city where a ban on low-level traffic stops went into effect.
sentences.zh: 费城在3月份成为第一个实施低级别交通拦截禁令的大城市。

sentences.en: The city council basically took a list of several low-level citations and said police can no longer stop you for these things.
sentences.zh: 市议会基本上列出了一系列低级别违规行为，并规定警察不能再因为这些事情拦下你。

sentences.en: Brooklyn Center, Minnesota, is working on a similar measure.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达州布鲁克林中心市正在制定类似的措施。

sentences.en: That's where Dante Wright, a young black man, was killed a year ago by an officer who grabbed her gun instead of her taser.
sentences.zh: 一年前，年轻的黑人男子丹特·赖特就是在那里被一名警察杀害的，那名警察错把枪当成了泰瑟枪。

sentences.en: In other places, we're seeing police commissions or police chiefs acting on their own.
sentences.zh: 在其他地方，我们看到警察委员会或警察局长在自行采取行动。

sentences.en: And other places around the country, it's the district attorneys who are taking action.
sentences.zh: 在全国其他地方，则是地方检察官在采取行动。

sentences.en: They're saying they want to reduce the incentives for these kinds of traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 他们表示希望减少进行此类交通拦截的动机。

sentences.en: So they're no longer going to bring charges based on contraband, drugs, or guns that are collected at pre-tech stops.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们将不再对在借口性拦截中收集到的违禁品、毒品或枪支提起指控。

sentences.en: The first DA to do that was in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 第一个这样做的地区检察官是在旧金山。

sentences.en: Most recently, the DA in Burlington,
sentences.zh: 最近，伯灵顿的地区检察官，

sentences.en: Vermont did something similar.
sentences.zh: 佛蒙特州也做了类似的事情。

sentences.en: And last fall, the district attorney in Ramsey County, Minnesota did the same thing.
sentences.zh: 去年秋天，明尼苏达州拉姆西县的地区检察官也采取了同样的行动。

sentences.en: People might remember that was where Philando Castile was killed a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 人们可能还记得，几年前费兰多·卡斯蒂利亚就是在那里被杀的。

sentences.en: He was a young black man who had politely told the officer pulling him over that he was carrying a handgun, which was licensed.
sentences.zh: 他是一名年轻的黑人男子，曾礼貌地告诉拦下他的警察，他携带了一把有执照的手枪。

sentences.en: And the officer nonetheless killed Mr. Castile when he reached for his identification.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，当卡斯蒂利亚先生伸手去拿身份证件时，警察还是杀了他。

sentences.en: David, has this reform faced any pushback?
sentences.zh: 大卫，这项改革是否面临阻力？

sentences.en: Yeah, there is vigorous pushback, most recently in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 是的，有强烈的阻力，最近是在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: Los Angeles is the biggest city yet to take some action to try to restrict or reduce low-level traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶是目前采取行动限制或减少低级别交通拦截的最大城市。

sentences.en: And what they've done there is actually fairly nuanced.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里所做的事情实际上相当微妙。

sentences.en: The police commission and the chief have asked officers to record themselves on their body camera
sentences.zh: 警察委员会和局长要求警察在随身摄像头上记录下自己

sentences.en: whenever they're pulling over a driver, explaining the real reason they're pulling over that driver.
sentences.zh: 在拦下司机时，解释他们拦下该司机的真实原因。

sentences.en: So that is, if an officer is pulling over a car with a broken taillight, the officer needs to make a recording explaining to the driver, look, it's not just your broken taillight.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果警察因为尾灯破损而拦下一辆车，警察需要录音向司机解释，看，不仅仅是因为你的尾灯坏了。

sentences.en: I also think your car resembles one that was recently associated with a serious crime or what have you.
sentences.zh: 我还认为你的车看起来像是一辆最近与严重犯罪有关的车，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And yet, even that
sentences.zh: 然而，即使是

sentences.en: relatively minor restriction on the ability of police to pull over cars has drawn quite a vigorous counterattack from the police union and its supporters.
sentences.zh: 对警察拦车能力的这种相对较小的限制，也遭到了警察工会及其支持者的强烈反击。

sentences.en: What are they saying?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Well, violent crime is everywhere in LA.
sentences.zh: 嗯，洛杉矶到处都是暴力犯罪。

sentences.en: Yet police commissioner Briggs voted to curtail LAPD's ability to keep guns off our streets.
sentences.zh: 然而警察专员布里格斯投票决定削减洛杉矶警察局将枪支从我们街头清除的能力。

sentences.en: The police union has put up online advertisements and its allies around Los Angeles are taking the
sentences.zh: 警察工会发布了在线广告，其在洛杉矶各地的盟友持有的

sentences.en: position that anything that discourages police from pulling over cars to look inside is going to have the result of keeping more guns and more criminals on the streets.
sentences.zh: 立场是，任何阻碍警察拦车搜查的行为，最终都会导致更多的枪支和罪犯留在街头。

sentences.en: Legal traffic and pedestrian stops take thousands of guns from criminals.
sentences.zh: 合法的交通和行人拦截从罪犯手中收缴了数千支枪支。

sentences.en: But Briggs claims that these stops don't curtail violent crime.
sentences.zh: 但布里格斯声称这些拦截并不能遏制暴力犯罪。

sentences.en: It's dishonest to say removing thousands of guns from LA doesn't curtail violence.
sentences.zh: 说从洛杉矶收缴数千支枪支不能遏制暴力是不诚实的。

sentences.en: This election, choose city leaders who work to keep guns off our streets.
sentences.zh: 这次选举，请选择致力于将枪支从我们街头清除的城市领导人。

sentences.en: What they're saying is that at a time when homicide rates are rising in Los Angeles and other cities, the last thing you want to do is put more hurdles in front of
sentences.zh: 他们说的是，在洛杉矶和其他城市凶杀率上升的时候，你最不应该做的就是给警察设置更多障碍，

sentences.en: the police and make a police officer think twice before he pulls over a car to check inside for drugs or guns or warrants.
sentences.zh: 让警察在拦车检查毒品、枪支或逮捕令之前三思而后行。

sentences.en: David, can you help me understand the dynamic here?
sentences.zh: 大卫，你能帮我理解这里的动态吗？

sentences.en: I mean, this is the police union going against rules that were set by the police chief, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是警察工会在反对警察局长制定的规则，对吧？

sentences.en: How do I understand that?
sentences.zh: 我该如何理解这一点？

sentences.en: Well, police unions represent their rank-and-file members who may see things differently than the management, their chiefs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，警察工会代表的是他们的基层成员，他们看待问题的角度可能与管理层或局长不同。

sentences.en: And that goes on in districts around the country.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在全国各地的地区都在发生。

sentences.en: So you often see police unions advocating for as much latitude as possible for the individual officers.
sentences.zh: 所以你经常看到警察工会主张为个别警察争取尽可能大的自由度。

sentences.en: They'd like to see as few rules restricting the officers as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们希望看到尽可能少的限制警察的规则。

sentences.en: And when officers get in trouble, the unions are there to defend them.
sentences.zh: 当警察遇到麻烦时，工会会站出来为他们辩护。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So worker versus management.
sentences.zh: 所以是员工与管理层的对立。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: The opponents of these reforms are arguing that it's just not going to work, that whatever benefits you might get, that's going to be outweighed by the loss of a really
sentences.zh: 这些改革的反对者认为这根本行不通，无论你可能获得什么好处，都将被失去一个真正

sentences.en: valuable crime-fighting tool.
sentences.zh: 有价值的打击犯罪工具所抵消。

sentences.en: The ability to pull over cars and take a look inside.
sentences.zh: 即拦车并进行搜查的能力。

sentences.en: So you have these two sides fighting.
sentences.zh: 所以现在双方在交锋。

sentences.en: Is there any real-world data to prove which side is right?
sentences.zh: 有没有任何现实世界的数据来证明哪一方是正确的？

sentences.en: So Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Seattle, Los Angeles, those are about to provide our first big city case studies.
sentences.zh: 费城、匹兹堡、西雅图、洛杉矶，这些城市即将提供我们首批大城市的案例研究。

sentences.en: But we do have an example in a small southern city about a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 但我们在大约十年前的一个南方小城市有一个例子。

sentences.en: There was a police chief there who on his own tried to implement reforms like this with some surprising results.
sentences.zh: 那里有一位警察局长，他独自尝试实施这样的改革，结果出人意料。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《纽约时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载该应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So David, tell me about this one police chief who implemented reforms on his own.
sentences.zh: 那么大卫，跟我讲讲那位独自实施改革的警察局长。

sentences.en: Well, that was Chief Harold Medlock of Fayetteville, North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是北卡罗来纳州费耶特维尔的局长哈罗德·梅德洛克。

sentences.en: Welcome to our conversation tonight on traffic stop disparities.
sentences.zh: 欢迎参加我们今晚关于交通拦截差异的对话。

sentences.en: We're excited to have this conversation with Harold Medlock, former deputy chief.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴能与前副局长哈罗德·梅德洛克进行这次对话。

sentences.en: There's actually a video of him telling a local nonprofit group how he set out to change the way his police officers do traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 实际上有一段视频，他在视频中告诉当地一个非营利组织，他是如何着手改变他的警察进行交通拦截的方式的。

sentences.en: Well, Kirsten, thanks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，克尔斯滕，谢谢。

sentences.en: And it's great to be with you tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚能和你在一起真是太好了。

sentences.en: About a decade ago, in 2013, he was new on the job.
sentences.zh: 大约十年前，即2013年，他刚上任。

sentences.en: He was the new chief in Fayetteville.
sentences.zh: 他是费耶特维尔的新局长。

sentences.en: And there had been a big issue in the city about what was known as driving while Black.
sentences.zh: 当时城市里有一个关于所谓的“黑人开车”的大问题。

sentences.en: The Black community felt that they had been subjected to discriminatory policing, especially behind the wheel.
sentences.zh: 黑人社区感到他们受到了歧视性的警务对待，特别是在开车时。

sentences.en: You know, we were doing a lot of work in 2013 in those first months and really
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在2013年的头几个月做了很多工作，确实

sentences.en: had started to think about how we were going to change our approach as police officers in Fayetteville.
sentences.zh: 开始思考我们作为费耶特维尔的警察将如何改变我们的方法。

sentences.en: So one morning around the time he was starting his job, Chief Medlock's wife comes home from Bible study.
sentences.zh: 有一天早上，就在梅德洛克局长刚开始这份工作的时候，他的妻子参加完圣经研习班回到家。

sentences.en: And she tells him a story.
sentences.zh: 她给他讲了一件事。

sentences.en: They began the Bible study that morning with some prayer time.
sentences.zh: 那天早上，他们以祈祷时间开始了圣经研习。

sentences.en: And as one lady began to talk, she broke down and started crying.
sentences.zh: 当一位女士开始说话时，她情绪崩溃，哭了起来。

sentences.en: Another woman, a Black woman, had broke out in tears.
sentences.zh: 另一位女性，一位黑人女性，也泪流满面。

sentences.en: Of course, the group stopped and said, well, what's wrong?
sentences.zh: 当然，大家停了下来，问她怎么了。

sentences.en: And she said, well, I was leaving home this morning, pulled out of my driveway, drove down to the end of my block, made the left.
sentences.zh: 她说，我今天早上离开家，把车开出车道，开到街区尽头，左转。

sentences.en: And as soon as I did, a Fayetteville police car stopped me.
sentences.zh: 我刚转过去，一辆费耶特维尔的警车就拦住了我。

sentences.en: This woman had been pulled over by one of the officers reporting to Chief Medlock.
sentences.zh: 这位女士被梅德洛克局长手下的一名警官拦下了。

sentences.en: And the officer walked up and asked her or told her that she had been stopped because she ran the stop sign.
sentences.zh: 警官走过来，问她或者告诉她，她被拦下是因为她闯了停车标志。

sentences.en: And then he said in a very abrupt tone, where are you going?
sentences.zh: 然后他用非常生硬的语气问，你要去哪儿？

sentences.en: And she said, well,
sentences.zh: 她说，嗯，

sentences.en: I'm going to a Bible study at Village Baptist Church.
sentences.zh: 我要去乡村浸信会教堂参加圣经研习。

sentences.en: The woman tried to explain that she lives in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这位女士试图解释她就住在附近。

sentences.en: She's not doing anything out of the ordinary.
sentences.zh: 她没做任何不寻常的事。

sentences.en: She's certainly not doing anything illegal.
sentences.zh: 她当然也没做任何违法的事。

sentences.en: But the officer won't let up.
sentences.zh: 但警官不依不饶。

sentences.en: And he said, again, very abruptly, well, there's no Bible studies going on at five o'clock in the morning on a Friday.
sentences.zh: 他又非常生硬地说，周五早上五点根本没有圣经研习。

sentences.en: So I need to know where you're going.
sentences.zh: 所以我得知道你要去哪儿。

sentences.en: And she said, well, I am going.
sentences.zh: 她说，我确实是要去。

sentences.en: If you'd like to follow me there, you're certainly welcome to.
sentences.zh: 如果你想跟着我过去，当然欢迎。

sentences.en: And he goes, I don't need to follow you there, but don't you run that stop sign anymore.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不需要跟着你，但你以后别再闯那个停车标志了。

sentences.en: And he turned around and left.
sentences.zh: 说完他转身就走了。

sentences.en: She was rattled by the encounter and she was shaken by the time she got to Bible study.
sentences.zh: 这次遭遇让她心烦意乱，到圣经研习班时她还在发抖。

sentences.en: And so at seven o'clock that morning, my wife comes in, shares that story and points a finger in my face and says, now, what are you going to do about it?
sentences.zh: 所以那天早上七点，我妻子进来分享了这个故事，指着我的脸说，现在，你打算怎么处理这件事？

sentences.en: So he gets to the station and he's steamed.
sentences.zh: 于是他到了警局，火冒三丈。

sentences.en: I do need to tell you that morning I went in and I was, I was on a rant.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，那天早上我进去的时候，我，我正在发火。

sentences.en: He wants to know who that officer was.
sentences.zh: 他想知道那个警官是谁。

sentences.en: I wanted him in my office before the close of business that day.
sentences.zh: 我要求他在当天下班前到我的办公室来。

sentences.en: And I want to know everything that we, we know about this traffic stop.
sentences.zh: 而且我想知道我们所知道的关于这次交通拦截的一切。

sentences.en: About three hours later, my internal affairs commander came back to me and said, chief, there is no record of that traffic stop.
sentences.zh: 大约三个小时后，我的内务部指挥官回来对我说，局长，没有这次交通拦截的记录。

sentences.en: The officer did not call it in.
sentences.zh: 那名警官没有上报。

sentences.en: He did not turn his car camera on.
sentences.zh: 他没有打开车上的摄像头。

sentences.en: There is no report of any radio traffic or any dispatch traffic.
sentences.zh: 没有任何无线电通话或调度记录。

sentences.en: That guy was out there playing the field.
sentences.zh: 那家伙当时在外面乱来。

sentences.en: He was, he was fishing, which made me even more angry.
sentences.zh: 他在，他在钓鱼执法，这让我更加生气。

sentences.en: And then he goes a step further and he decides to start telling all the officers to quit pulling over drivers for harmless offenses like expired registration or a
sentences.zh: 然后他更进一步，决定开始告诉所有警官，停止拦截那些因无害违规行为（如注册过期）的司机，或者

sentences.en: broken taillight or some obstruction in the window.
sentences.zh: 尾灯损坏，或者车窗有遮挡物。

sentences.en: From now on, I only want you pulling over cars for dangerous moving violations that might pose a risk to other drivers.
sentences.zh: 从现在起，我只要求你们拦截那些可能对其他司机造成风险的危险交通违规行为。

sentences.en: And he meets with a firestorm.
sentences.zh: 结果他遭到了猛烈的抨击。

sentences.en: There was a lot of anger and angst and frustration that I was taking a tool away from them that was going to cause crime and Fayetteville to go up.
sentences.zh: 大家非常愤怒、焦虑和沮丧，认为我剥夺了他们的一项工具，这会导致费耶特维尔的犯罪率上升。

sentences.en: The officers in his department all predict that if they have to stop pulling cars over on minor pretext, poke around for drugs or guns,
sentences.zh: 他部门的警官们都预测，如果他们不能再以琐碎的借口拦截车辆，去搜查毒品或枪支，

sentences.en: Fayetteville is going to see an explosion of violence and drug crime.
sentences.zh: 费耶特维尔将迎来暴力和毒品犯罪的爆发。

sentences.en: So this sounds like the exact same argument the unions were making against the current reforMs.
sentences.zh: 这听起来和工会反对当前改革的论点完全一样。

sentences.en: But is there any truth to this argument?
sentences.zh: 但这个论点有道理吗？

sentences.en: It's exactly the same argument.
sentences.zh: 这完全是同一个论点。

sentences.en: And in the case of Fayetteville, there really isn't any evidence to support it.
sentences.zh: 而在费耶特维尔的案例中，确实没有任何证据支持它。

sentences.en: The North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation collects data on traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳州调查局收集了交通拦截的数据。

sentences.en: And what that data shows is that during the three or four years that Chief Medlock was in charge, the number of traffic stops went way up, mostly for moving violations.
sentences.zh: 数据显示，在梅德洛克局长任职的三四年里，交通拦截的数量大幅上升，主要是针对交通违规。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the number of searches of black motorists went way down.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，对黑人司机的搜查次数大幅下降。

sentences.en: And none of these things appeared to have any impact either way on homicides, violent crime or drug crime.
sentences.zh: 而这些变化似乎对杀人案、暴力犯罪或毒品犯罪都没有任何影响。

sentences.en: So the predictions of an explosion in these kinds of offenses, if the police lost this tool to try to search cars, none of that came to pass.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果警察失去了搜查车辆的工具，犯罪率会爆发的预测，并没有成为现实。

sentences.en: And it's made Chief Medlock a big name in policing.
sentences.zh: 这让梅德洛克局长在警界名声大噪。

sentences.en: The Obama administration attorney general came to Fayetteville to see what he was up to.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马政府的司法部长曾来到费耶特维尔，看看他在做什么。

sentences.en: And since then, a lot of people around the country, city councils, police chiefs, district attorneys, have called on Chief Medlock to give them advice
sentences.zh: 从那以后，全国各地的许多人，包括市议会、警察局长、地方检察官，都请求梅德洛克局长为他们提供建议，

sentences.en: about how he turned things around in Fayetteville.
sentences.zh: 关于他是如何扭转费耶特维尔局面的。

sentences.en: So his experiment worked?
sentences.zh: 所以他的实验成功了？

sentences.en: It seemed to.
sentences.zh: 看起来是这样。

sentences.en: But it's worth noting that since he left the job in 2016, there are some signs that things have turned back in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 但值得注意的是，自他2016年离职以来，有一些迹象表明情况又回到了原来的方向。

sentences.en: The African-American community in Fayetteville has begun complaining again that black motorists are being stopped disproportionately.
sentences.zh: 费耶特维尔的非裔美国人社区再次开始抱怨黑人司机受到不成比例的拦截。

sentences.en: The number of searches of black drivers and passengers has risen.
sentences.zh: 对黑人司机和乘客的搜查次数有所上升。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the number of traffic stops for dangerous offenses like speeding has actually declined.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，针对超速等危险违规行为的交通拦截数量实际上有所下降。

sentences.en: So it sounds like there are these questions about whether the policies Medlock put into place actually survived.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来，关于梅德洛克实施的政策是否真正延续下来，存在这些疑问。

sentences.en: You know, whether the people who came in after him continued them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是在他之后接任的人是否继续执行了这些政策。

sentences.en: It seems like this points to how strong the forces are that are preventing reform.
sentences.zh: 这似乎表明阻碍改革的力量有多么强大。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering, what does that tell us about what's going to happen, you know, in these other jurisdictions you told us about?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，这告诉我们关于你提到的其他司法管辖区将会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, at this point, it's all very uncertain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，目前一切都非常不确定。

sentences.en: You know, certainly there are people around law enforcement who write off Fayetteville as an anomaly and suggest that those practices can't be extended
sentences.zh: 你知道，当然有一些执法界的人把费耶特维尔的情况视为特例，并认为这些做法无法在

sentences.en: elsewhere with the same results.
sentences.zh: 其他地方推广并获得同样的结果。

sentences.en: Or even more commonly, they say, look, maybe most pretextual stops don't do any good, but a few of them do a lot of good.
sentences.zh: 或者更常见的是，他们说，看，也许大多数借口性拦截没什么用，但其中少数确实很有用。

sentences.en: And in this context, with murder rates rising around the country, even one extra gun on the streets is too many.
sentences.zh: 在这种背景下，随着全国谋杀率的上升，即使街上多出一把枪也是太多了。

sentences.en: So what we're seeing is that in places like San Francisco, the police union is backing a recall effort against the district
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到，在旧金山等地，警察工会正在支持罢免当地的地方检察官，

sentences.en: attorney there, who was one of the first to try to stop pressing charges around contraband collected at pretextual stops.
sentences.zh: 他是第一批试图停止对借口性拦截中查获的违禁品进行起诉的人之一。

sentences.en: We're seeing the police union in Philadelphia has filed a lawsuit claiming that the
sentences.zh: 我们看到费城的警察工会提起诉讼，声称

sentences.en: local statute restricting minor traffic stops conflicts with the state law on traffic violations.
sentences.zh: 限制轻微交通拦截的地方法规与州交通违规法律相冲突。

sentences.en: In Virginia, two years ago, the Democrats controlled the statehouse and passed one of the first statewide measures to restrict minor traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 在弗吉尼亚州，两年前，民主党控制了州议会，并通过了首批限制轻微交通拦截的州级措施之一。

sentences.en: Now we're seeing Republicans try to roll that back with the help of the Republican attorney general and a number of law enforcement associations and officials around the state.
sentences.zh: 现在我们看到共和党人在共和党总检察长和州内一些执法协会及官员的帮助下，试图推翻这些措施。

sentences.en: So really, it's up for grabs whether any of these reforms are going to stick around or what kind of effect they're ultimately going to have.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些改革是否能坚持下去，或者最终会产生什么样的影响，真的很难说。

sentences.en: David, stepping back for a moment here, over the past few years, as we know, there's been this big
sentences.zh: 大卫，退一步说，过去几年，正如我们所知，美国一直在进行一场关于警务的重大

sentences.en: public conversation about policing in the United States, in some ways starting with the killing of
sentences.zh: 公众对话，在某种程度上始于2020年明尼阿波利斯的乔治·弗洛伊德被杀事件。

sentences.en: George Floyd in Minneapolis in 2020.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，两年后的今天，这些努力看起来怎么样？

sentences.en: And I guess I'm wondering now, two years later, what those efforts look like?
sentences.zh: 它们发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: What's happened to them?
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，暴力犯罪和谋杀率正在上升？

sentences.en: When, as you said, violent crime and murder rates are rising?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们现在正处于一个真正的碰撞时刻，一方面是乔治·弗洛伊德被杀后运动中产生的对警察改革的需求，

sentences.en: Well, we're in a real moment of collision right now between those demands for police reform that grew
sentences.zh: 另一方面，全国各地对犯罪率上升的恐惧。

sentences.en: out of the movement after the killing of George Floyd on the one hand, and on the other hand, a lot of fear from the rising crime rates around the country.
sentences.zh: 这使得任何试图限制警察在工作中行使权力的努力在政治上都变得危险。

sentences.en: And that has made any effort to try to restrict the ability of police to do what they want on the job politically perilous.
sentences.zh: 一些在全国范围内最积极推动这些交通警务改革的官员，

sentences.en: Some of the officials who were most active in trying to implement these reforms to traffic policing around the country
sentences.zh: 实际上不愿在公开场合与我交谈，因为他们担心这会使他们成为政治反对派的目标。

sentences.en: were actually reluctant to talk to me on the record because they were afraid that that would make them targets of the political opposition.
sentences.zh: 他们已经感受到了指责的压力，即通过限制警察拦截车辆的能力，他们正在助长犯罪率上升并使

sentences.en: They're already feeling the stings of accusations that by restricting the ability of officers to pull over cars, they're contributing to rising crime rates and putting
sentences.zh: 人们处于危险之中。

sentences.en: people at risk.
sentences.zh: 他们担心如果与这些改革挂钩，下次选举会更困难，或者更难保住工作。

sentences.en: And they're afraid that if they get associated with that, it's going to be harder for them at the next election or harder for them to stay in their jobs.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到，一方面是对变革的恐惧。

sentences.en: So what we're seeing is, on the one hand, this sort of fear of change.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们看到一些大城市正在尝试从根本上重新思考他们的交通拦截方式。

sentences.en: And on the other hand, we're seeing some of the largest cities in the country try to fundamentally rethink their approach to traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 很快我们就会有来自全国各地的数据，显示这些实验的结果是否与费耶特维尔的经验相符。

sentences.en: Soon we'll have data from around the country showing whether the results of those experiments match the experience of Fayetteville.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，犯罪学家早就有了数据表明，借口性拦截可能不是警察打击犯罪的最佳方式。

sentences.en: But at the same time, criminologists have had data for a while showing that pretextual stops may not be the best way for police to fight crime.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些实验即使有数据支持，能否产生长期效果，最终还是要取决于政治。

sentences.en: And so whether these experiments, even with data, yield long-term results is going to come down to politics.
sentences.zh: 考虑到目前的阻力和上升的犯罪率，它们是否会被证明是昙花一现，还有待观察。

sentences.en: And given the headwinds right now and the rising crime rates, whether they prove to be short-lived remains to be seen.
sentences.zh: 大卫，谢谢你。

sentences.en: David, thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 周日，埃马纽埃尔·马克龙赢得了法国总统的第二个任期，以相当大的优势击败了极右翼挑战者玛丽娜·勒庞。

sentences.en: On Sunday, Emmanuel Macron won a second term as president of France, beating his far-right challenger, Marine Le Pen, by a substantial margin.
